newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday on speculative buying mainly from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at 3,374 yuan ($407) per tonne, rising 66 yuan. It opened at 3,375 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,376 and a low of 3,370.
May rose three yuan to 3,308, September 67 to 3,385, November six to 3,388 and the January 1998 contract fell 12 to 3,380.
Combined volume fell to 11,900 tonnes from 39,700.
Soybeans opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Retail investors dominated today's trading but other investors would rather stay on the sidelines ahead of the weekend," one trader said.
"Soybeans have moved in a range of 3,300 and 3,400 for a long time and it is likely the trend will continue in the short term due to a lack of market-moving news," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to meet strong resistance at the 3,400-yuan level in the next few days.
